holidays.name: Eat an Extra Dessert Day
holidays.description: A day that gives you permission to add a second dessert to your plate. Order the cheesecake and the brownie sundae, and skip the guilt.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on sweet-tooth calendars.
holidays.funFact: The word 'dessert' comes from the French 'desservir', which means 'to clear the table'. Dessert was originally what came after the table was cleared.

holidays.name: National Macadamia Nut Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the buttery, crunchy, rich macadamia nut. Eat them in cookies, roast them with salt, or crack into a jar of them.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors one of the world's most prized nuts.
holidays.funFact: Macadamia nuts are native to Australia, but Hawaii made them famous. The shells are so hard that cracking them takes about 300 pounds of pressure.

holidays.name: National Wildlife Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate animals in the wild, from backyard squirrels to elephants, and to think about protecting their habitats.
holidays.origin: Animal advocate and pet lifestyle expert Colleen Paige founded it in 2005. She started it in memory of Steve Irwin, the Australian conservationist known as the Crocodile Hunter, who died in 2006.
holidays.funFact: Colleen Paige created the day to raise awareness of endangered species. Many fans now mark it with wildlife documentaries and donations to conservation groups.
